newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Placer makes new offer to Highlands.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer makes new offer to Highlands.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Monday it was offering to cancel its stake in Highlands Gold Ltd for Highlands' 25-percent stake in the Porgera gold project in Papua New Guinea.

Highlands said earlier on Monday that its directors had unanimously resolved to reject a takeover bid by Placer Dome, citing an independent report showing Highlands shares to be worth about 40 percent more than the 75 cent per share offer price.
The Canadian company has about 33 percent of the PNG miner. Both companies have 25-percent stakes in the Porgera gold mine, which produces about one million ounces a year.
Placer chief executive and president John Willson said the latest offer was being made in response to the valuation in the report prepared by Barings.

"I see this as the only solution possible to deliver Highlands Gold shareholders the value that their independent expert believes in in Frieda-Nena, Ramu and the exploration assets," Willson said, referring to other PNG mine prospects.
"Placer Dome cannot accept these valuations and is unable to justify any increase in its takeover offer, let alone the 21 cents necessary to bring the offer into Barings' valuation range," he added.

"The Barings valuation of Highlands' 25 per cent interest in Porgera is inconsistent with the valuation Barings completed just 18 months ago. However, we are prepared to concede that the issue regarding valuation of Porgera may be bridged and are making a proposal to do so," Willson said in a statement.
He said that the valuations of Frieda-Nena and Ramu were beyond his comprehension, and Placer Dome could not ascribe "even a fraction" of the value given by Barings to those assets.
Placer would be prepared to buy 25 percent of Porgera at the mid-point of the Barings valuation range, or A$276.8 million, he said.
It would also purchase Highlands receivables from the Papua New Guinea government relating to Porgera on the same terms.
Willson described the proposal as a "win win" solution.
Placer said any difference in the value of the Porgera stake and its own stake in Highlands could be settled in cash.

"Highlands Gold shareholders would get to keep the assets that Highlands' directors apparently value so highly but which Placer Dome cannot agree to pay for," he said. "Placer Dome would buy 25 percent of Porgera, an operation it knows and understands at the value ascribed by the independent expert."
Mining analyst Greg Foulis at BZW Australia Limited said: "Placer has always take the view that they're only really interested in Porgera...They don't want the rest."
The announcement came after the close of trading. Highlands Gold's shares closed at 77 cents, up two cents on Friday's close.
